record.context_brief: Conformal cosmology and the universe-age problem
record.original_question: Can a cosmological term naturally of the same order of magnitude as the cosmological particle-energy density resolve the age problem of the Universe within conformal cosmology? The issue is whether a cosmological term induced by scale breaking in a traceless conformal energy-momentum tensor can be explored in enough detail to account for observations suggesting that the Universe may be younger than some of its constituents.

evidence.quote: And third, if any cosmological term is induced in Tµν as a consequence of the scale breaking Higgs mechanism which is needed to induce masses into the conformal invariant theory in the first place, then since the conformal Tµν is traceless (and remains so even after the symmetry breaking), any induced cosmological term would have to be of the same order of magnitude as all the other terms in Tµν which for cosmology would mean the energy density of the particles in the Universe.

Moreover, while it still needs to be explored in detail, a cosmological constant term of order of magnitude the cosmological energy density might provide a solution to the current age problem of the Universe, with recent astrophysical measurements indicating an age for the Universe which may be less than that of some of its constituents.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a conformal-invariant theory of gravitation in which matter is coupled to a traceless energy–momentum tensor $T_{\mu
u}$ (so $g^{\mu
u}T_{\mu
u}=0$), and in which particle masses are generated dynamically through a scale-breaking Higgs mechanism that preserves the tracelessness of $T_{\mu
u}$. Because $T_{\mu
u}$ remains traceless after symmetry breaking, any cosmological-constant term $\Lambda g_{\mu
u}$ that is induced as a consequence of this scale breaking must be of the same order of magnitude as the other contributions to $T_{\mu
u}$; in a cosmological setting this means $\Lambda$ is naturally of order the energy density $ho$ of the particles in the Universe.

Within the Robertson–Walker cosmology derived from such a conformal theory, with Hubble parameter $H_0$ and matter density of order $ho$, determine whether the inclusion of an induced cosmological-constant term of order $ho$ produces a present-day age of the Universe large enough to exceed the inferred ages of the oldest astrophysical constituents (e.g. globular clusters). That is, show whether a cosmological term of magnitude $|\Lambda|\sim ho$, arising from the scale-breaking mechanism in the traceless conformal $T_{\mu
u}$, resolves the cosmological age problem in conformal cosmology.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work in conformal cosmology (notably astro-ph/9601071 and later papers) developed this idea in detail and argued that an induced cosmological term of order the matter density does yield an age of the Universe of order 1/H_0, alleviating the age problem. The proposal is therefore partially developed/affirmed within that framework, though it has not been definitively resolved as a generally accepted resolution of the age problem outside conformal gravity.

status_evidence.title: Conformal cosmology and the age of the universe
status_evidence.snippet: Explicit study of conformal cosmology addressing the age of the Universe.
status_evidence.claim: Follow-up work explicitly explored whether conformal cosmology with an induced cosmological term resolves the age problem.

status_evidence.title: Conformal gravity and a natural solution to the cosmological constant problem
status_evidence.snippet: Cosmological constant naturally of order the energy density of ordinary matter without fine tuning.
status_evidence.claim: Conformal gravity yields a cosmological term of order the matter density, supporting the proposed resolution.
